referents.why: 'your word' is second masculine singular inside Moses' reply; the word he points back to is Pharaoh's 'tomorrow', so the addressee of this speech is Pharaoh
referents.category: second person inside a reply, addressee of that speech

referents.why: 'our' is first common plural in Moses' speech; it cannot be Moses alone, and Pharaoh (the addressee, who is told to know the LORD) is excluded; the nearest plural group on Moses' side is Moses and Aaron, who were both summoned. The builder's 'he' is singular and fails the morphology
referents.category: first person plural inside speech, speaker's own side

referents.why: the clause answers Moses' question 'When shall I pray?' with 'tomorrow'; the one asked, and the one who gave the honor, is Pharaoh, so the act decides over nearest-noun order (Moses was the last named speaker)
referents.category: implied subject of an answer, set by the act not the nearest noun

referents.why: wayyiqtol 'he said' replying to Pharaoh's answer; the speaker who changes is Moses, whose speech is 'according to your word' addressed to Pharaoh
referents.category: implied subject, change of speaker in a dialogue exchange

referents.why: 'you may know' is second masculine singular in Moses' speech; the person addressed, and the one whose word is accepted, is Pharaoh
referents.category: implied you inside a speech, addressee of that speech

links.why: cl5 states what Pharaoh is to know (yada, 'that there is no one like the LORD'); it is the object of knowing, not a reason
cl4 is inside Moses' speech; 'and then' runs only along the narrative line of wayyiqtol clauses, and this yiqtol with lemaan is not a next event after Pharaoh's 'he said'
links.category: speech clause read as narrative sequence

links.why: cl1 ('tomorrow') is inside Pharaoh's speech, not on the narrative line; the wayyiqtol cl2 continues from the saying clause cl0, not from what was said
links.category: speech clause read as narrative sequence

links.why: lemaan + yiqtol in a different person (you) after the wish 'according to your word': the assent is for the sake of Pharaoh's knowing; the form is outside the literal lists but the sense is purpose
links.category: purpose clause after an elliptical wish

links.why: cl0 is the speaking clause and cl1 'tomorrow' is what Pharaoh said; the said fragment sits inside the saying
cl2 is the speaking clause and cl3 is the first of the words Moses said
the second wayyiqtol 'he said' follows the first on the narrative line, one speaker answering the other
'according to your word' (ke + dabar) points back to Pharaoh's saying 'tomorrow': Moses declares his reply the fulfilment of Pharaoh's word

groups.why: Pharaoh's answer is addressed to Moses, who has just asked 'When?'; the builder gave no addressee
Moses' reply is addressed to Pharaoh ('your word', 'you may know'); the builder gave no addressee

none_fit.what: a verbless assent or wish ('so be it, as you say') has no group kind or link type of its own; it is not a command (no imperative group) and its relation to Pharaoh's 'tomorrow' is closest to 'as' but is a prepositional phrase rather than a clause
lemaan + yiqtol after a wish is a purpose, but the purpose type is defined for a command followed by waw + jussive or for lamed + infinitive

cant_tell.what: whether 'our' in 'the LORD our God' is Moses and Aaron or Moses with all Israel
cant_tell.why: the text gives only a first person plural; Moses and Aaron is the only composite on offer and agrees in number, but Israel is also plausible

cant_tell.what: whether cl3 carries an elided verb (likely a jussive 'let it be') that would make it a command
cant_tell.why: the parse gives no verb; no imperative group is added because the list cannot confirm a command
